clauses.reason: Section 2 requires the Secretary of State to consult listed officials to ensure compatibility between the Foreign Service personnel system and other government personnel systems. It is a standing duty with no end. Amendments, with before and after wording: EO 12388 section 4 (effective August 24, 1982) struck International Communication Agency and inserted United States Information Agency; EO 13118 section 10(4)(A) (effective April 1, 1999 under its section 11) struck Director of the United States International Development Cooperation Agency and inserted Administrator of the United States Agency for International Development; EO 13374 section 2 (signed March 14, 2005, no effective date stated) strikes the phrase the Director of the International Communication Agency, the Director of the United States International Development Cooperation Agency and inserts the Administrator of the United States Agency for International Development. The phrase EO 13374 strikes no longer matched the section text after EO 12388 and EO 13118, so the held text does not show exactly how that strike operated; every version keeps the consultation duty, so the clause continues as amended.

clauses.reason: Section 4 establishes the salary classes for the Senior Foreign Service. Note for the reviewer: the substance of this section was replaced. The original set each class at basic pay equivalent to Senior Executive Service levels ES 1 to ES 6 (Career Minister at ES 6; Minister-Counselor at ES 4 to ES 6; Counselor at ES 1 to ES 6). EO 13325 (January 23, 2004; its stated effective date is the first day of the first applicable pay period beginning on or after January 1, 2004, a calendar date the held text does not give, so January 1, 2004 is recorded as the earliest date that formula allows) restated section 4 to read as ranges tied to Executive Schedule level III and GS-15. EO 13374 section 1 (signed March 14, 2005, no effective date stated) restated section 4 again as ranges from the minimum senior-level rate under 5 U.S.C. 5376 up to stated percentages of Executive Schedule levels II and III, and its section 3 revoked EO 13325. Under the strike-and-insert ruling the clause continues, amended, with section 4 as restated by EO 13374.

research_rationale:
EO 12293 (signed February 23, 1981; 46 FR 13969) implements the Foreign Service Act of 1980: it delegates functions to the Secretary of State (section 1), sets consultation and recommendation duties (sections 2 and 3), establishes Senior Foreign Service salary classes (section 4), delegates transitional pay authority (section 5), establishes the Board of Examiners (section 6), provides for retirement information (section 7) and sets the effective date (section 8). I read the complete held Federal Register original. I corrected the dossier inventory: section 4 and its duplicated OCR pay-rate lines are one clause, section 6(d) is cut before section 7, and section 7 is added (14 clauses). Six held later orders are attached with before and after wording: EO 12363 (adds sections 9 and 10, limits section 8), EO 12388 and EO 13118 (agency names in sections 2 and 9), EO 12536 (revokes section 9(e), an added paragraph), EO 13325 and EO 13374 (successive restatements of section 4; EO 13374 revokes EO 13325 and also amends section 2). Sections 9 and 10 exist only in EO 12363, not in the original, so they are described in the section 8 clause, and the one end among them is the revocation of section 9(e) by EO 12536 on October 9, 1985. The OFR disposition entry lists the amendments by EO 12363, 12388, 12536, 13118 and 13374 and no revocation; the FR notice 06-9855 refers to the order as amended and reprinted in the 22 U.S.C. 3901 note. No held later order revokes or supersedes EO 12293. The bounded searches record no revocation or supersession. All fourteen original clauses are operative as amended, checked through 2026-10-14. Disclosed limits: section 5 is transitional and no held source shows its authority exhausted, so it is recorded as not ended; the phrase EO 13374 strikes from section 2 no longer matched the section text, so how that strike operated is not shown.
